source._note: RE-SOURCED 2026-07-25 from the REAL High Plains Raceway at 93301 E US Hwy 36, Deer Trail CO (39.7353,-103.8980). Replaces fabricated compressed lat/lon traced off the old unified map (which placed it at 39.67,-104.77, ~70 km away). Geometry is the closed cycle of OSM highway=raceway ways: Short North, Bikers Berm, Niagara, Dannys Lesson, High Plains Drifter, Prarie Corkscrew, Full West + one unnamed link = 3220 m (2.00 mi). The north section (To Hell On A Bobsled / Ladder To Heaven) is EXCLUDED: its south end is unmapped in OSM, leaving a 110 m gap that would have to be invented to close the full 2.55-mile course (LAWS L1 — never invent geometry). Add it by tracing that 110 m off a georeferenced aerial, then re-chain. Pit Lane excluded (not the racing line). Winding CW to match the other CO circuits. Elevation from USGS 3DEP at the real site.
source._width_note: default_width_m 12.0 is INHERITED FROM THE FABRICATED CONFIG and unverified against the real circuit.

The projection snaps to the nearest ring vertex.
route._orientation_doc: Research 2026-07-20: High Plains Raceway runs CLOCKWISE (PCA turn guide + LapMeta, 15 turns, 2.56 mi). Our ring is already CW. REAL S/F: mid front straight (~370 m, WSW->ENE ~102 deg, between the Prairie Corkscrew exit and T1) at real-world ~39.7350,-103.8946 — but THIS trace lives in a displaced frame (~77 km off; re-source pending per CLAUDE.md), so start_at is the matching straight IN THE TRACE'S OWN FRAME: the 207 m straight bearing 115.7 deg, midpoint 39.67456,-104.77141. Re-derive when re-sourced. Pit lane: real hot pits on the NORTH side of the front straight (driver's left), ~690 m incl. entry/exit; entry before S/F at the corkscrew exit, exit wraps outside T1-T2 and merges at T2 exit.

road_wear._doc: ledger 0084 'High Plains 0.1.7' (Kevin 2026-11-07: "road textures to include wear along where tires run, in a realistic manner" / "sampling the entire road's texture from aerial data and mapping it directly onto the entire road" / "For tracks we'll use racing lines" / "Which will help darken curbs realistically"; 2026-11-08: "the road texture from aerial isn't done yet"; 2026-11-10: "lets continue, drives looked good"). Milford 0.1.7's bake (tools/road_wear_blend.py, last in prep): the large-scale tone off NAIP 2023 0.3 m, registered to the built road, under the stock cracked asphalt kept as the 4 m detail (ksPerPixelMultiMap_NMDetail); the rubber is the photo's own (rubber 'photo', below: no drawn band); the traced race kerbs get the photo's measured darkening where the line rides them (kerbs, below). scripts/aerial/road_wear.py DEFAULTS has every number, marked measured / model / invented.

The race kerbs are not a surface here: they keep their own paint (kerbs)
road_wear._texel_doc: PC 2026-11-10 (ledger 0084 'High Plains 0.1.7'): 0.25 m. 0.2 m broke the detail phase: 4096 px x 0.2 / 4 = 204.8, not whole, and the flipped v put the grain 0.8 tile off the prep's 4 m phase (both PC builds red on road_wear_check detail_phase, 0.20001 tiles); 0.25 m makes it 256, whole (Milford's), with 80 m cells = 320 px (12 x 12 = 144 slots for the 74 cells), and is still finer than the photo's 0.3 m pixel, so no tone it carries is lost. Was: the aerial is NAIP 2023 at 0.30 m (Milford's 0.50 m gave 0.25). 0.2 m: finer than the source pixel, so every tone the 0.3 m photo carries is kept, and a whole divisor of the 4 m detail tile (the cell, margin and pitch stay whole tiles, so the grain keeps the prep's 4 m grid and phase; 0.15 m, half the pixel, is not: 26.7 texels a tile). The next finer divisor, 0.125 m, needs an 8192 px atlas (4x the VRAM of Milford's 4096) for what the photo can no longer resolve; 0.2 m fits 4096 on the centreline's own cells (78 of 81 tiles, estimated off data/centerline.local.json)
road_wear._rubber_doc: Kevin 2026-11-10: "Use the photo's rubber" (ledger 0084 'High Plains 0.1.7: the photo's rubber'). NAIP 2023 at 0.3 m resolves it: lit asphalt within 0.5 m of the model line reads 0.915 of the lit median, the same distance from its mirror across the centreline 1.075 (source/road_wear/mac_read/naip_read.log). So the asphalt gets NO drawn band, the photo's tone carries the rubber; the bake measures the photo's darkening across the line against its mirror (scripts/aerial/road_wear.photo_rubber) and the kerbs take that measured profile through their 16 levels instead of the drawn model (amplitude 0.22, spread 0.70 m, base 0.35: unused here). The min-curvature line stays only to measure that and to say which kerb faces it clips. The default for the other 0.3 m circuits (Pueblo, Aspen, Grand Junction, Pikes Peak) when they get road wear; Milford (0.5 m, <= 1 % seen) keeps the drawn band

kerbs._doc: ledger 0081's 20 traced kerb runs (tools/author_kerbs_blend.py, 1KERB_circuit_<k>: blue / white kerbs and blue / yellow paint stripes, kerb_atlas_hp.png): 18 of them lie partly over the lane (data/kerbs.built.json in_vs_ribbon_edge_m < 0) at their measured offsets, where the line's tyres run. Each face takes the photo's measured darkening at its centroid's signed offset from the line (rubber 'photo'), to one of 16 copies of its own paint (copy k = paint x (1 - k x the measured peak / 15)), its u moved into that copy (v, the stripes, untouched); the material row is the exporter's own (ksPerPixel, no VAR) with txDiffuse -> the levelled paint. 16 levels [invented]: a 1.5 % step
